overview.title: climasusDB: an open integrated database for climate, health and environment
overview.lede: climasusDB organizes public health, climate and environmental data into a local-first platform that can be queried in the browser and published to cloud storage. Its goal is to support analysis, visualization, applied research and product development in the climaSUS ecosystem.
overview.institution_body: climasusDB is part of the Rondônia Climate and Health Center and the broader climaSUS ecosystem. Development is funded by INCT-Conexão, with a focus on open infrastructure for analyzing climate risks and health outcomes in Brazil.

sections.title: What climasusDB is
body: It is the data component of climaSUS: an organized, versioned and documented layer that transforms public systems into analysis-ready datasets.

Health data primarily comes from DATASUS; climate data includes observational sources such as INMET and, when published, gridded sources such as ERA5, CHIRPS, PRODES and CAMS. Methodological transformation is handled by the climasus4r package.

sections.title: How it is structured
body: The architecture follows bronze, silver and gold layers. Bronze preserves raw or near-raw data; silver standardizes keys, dates and variables; gold publishes stable Parquet tables with provenance metadata embedded in the Arrow schema.

The data/public directory is exactly the layout intended for publication in a public bucket. The web app reads catalog.json and queries Parquet files through HTTP Range requests using DuckDB-WASM, without its own backend.

sections.title: Data formats
body: Parquet is the official canonical format for climasusDB. It preserves types, compresses well, works with DuckDB, R and Python, and supports efficient partial reads in the browser.
ZIP-compressed CSV is offered only for small or summarized datasets. XLSX is not published in the catalog because it is redundant, less suitable for versioning and fragile for large datasets.

sections.title: Publishing and citation
body: Operational data hosting should use a public bucket, such as Google Cloud Storage or Cloudflare R2. Zenodo should be used for archiving, DOI assignment and citation of closed releases.
This separation avoids using Zenodo as the atlas backend while preserving a citable, permanent and auditable copy of published data.

product_sections.title: Explore
body: The main interactive analysis area. It supports navigation by municipality, state, indicator group and time series, using DuckDB queries directly over the published Parquet files.

product_sections.title: Data Catalog
body: A navigable repository of published datasets. It shows version, schema, provenance, coverage and download links. Parquet is always available; zipped CSV appears only for small or summarized datasets.

product_sections.title: Applications
body: A space for third-party or partner products that shared applications, dashboards, studies or prototypes built with climasusDB data or other products from the climaSUS ecosystem.

product_sections.title: Documentation
body: A reference page for understanding the institutional origin, architecture, data contracts, query logic and technical paths for reproduction and publication.

data-model.title: Data model & provenance
body: Every Gold dataset published under data/public/gold/ is a Parquet file with provenance metadata embedded in the Arrow schema, under the "climasus_meta" key (written by climasus4r::write_parquet_climasus()). This metadata includes the source DATASUS system, pipeline stage, aggregation type, and a processing history.

Versioning follows vX.Y.Z per dataset (e.g. health_climate_daily/v1.0.0). The path is always gold/{dataset}/v{version}/uf={uf}/data.parquet — the schema is identical between synthetic and real versions, so nothing in the frontend needs to change when a dataset moves from prototype to real data.
data/public/catalog.json lists every published dataset; each has a sibling datapackage.json (Frictionless Data standard) with the full schema and the same provenance metadata.

querying.title: Querying with DuckDB-WASM
body: climasusDB has no backend: the browser runs a WebAssembly build of DuckDB and queries the published Parquet files directly via HTTP range requests — only the bytes needed for each query are downloaded.

The same Parquet files can be opened outside the platform, with no dependency on climasusDB at all: with the DuckDB CLI (SELECT * FROM read_parquet('URL')), with pandas/pyarrow in Python, or with arrow::read_parquet() in R.
Example query used by Explore: SELECT code_muni, avg(tmax) FROM health_climate_daily GROUP BY code_muni.

catalog-contract.title: Catalog contract
body: catalog.json guarantees: dataset name, latest version, list of available versions, synthetic-data flag, relative Parquet path, and row count. datapackage.json guarantees the column schema and the full climasus_meta metadata.

Tabular datasets (like health_climate_daily) use this Frictionless Data contract, not STAC. The STAC catalog (build_stac.R) is reserved for future gridded raster datasets (ERA5, CHIRPS) once those are published — this avoids duplicating two cataloging systems for the same tabular data type.

heat-cardio.title: Heat and mortality in Rondônia
body: This theme applies to Rondônia's published data the same methodological approach from a climasus4r case study on cardiovascular mortality in the elderly and heatwaves: detect heatwave events (WHO/WMO methods) from INMET station temperature series and relate them to the daily death series per municipality.

The published datasets backing this theme are health_climate_daily (daily deaths and climate per municipality, 2018–2023) and heatwave_events (heatwave events detected at RO's INMET stations, with a severity index and intensity class).
For the full statistical methodology (DLNM, attributable burden), see the corresponding advanced-modeling tutorial in the climasus4r documentation.
